note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 100, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Approve the exact whole battle after restoring its 15–16 October 1793 extent. The Hauts-de-France Inventaire record explicitly gives both days, and the Ministry of Culture identifies Jourdan opposite Clerfayt’s Austrian army. CDB90 represents the French Army of the North and the Austrian force at this engagement as two aggregate armies (44000/23000 initial personnel), not the whole First Coalition or all forces besieging Maubeuge. The institutional records establish the event, dates and opposed commands; they do not independently certify the tabulated counts or the 4500/3000 casualty estimates. No siege-garrison count is added. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name FRENCH ARMY OF THE NORTH): Original CDB90 FRENCH ARMY OF THE NORTH, localized and bounded to Wattignies. Ministry of Culture evidence identifies Jourdan, with Carnot and Duquesnoy; no separate commander or garrison strength is created. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name AUSTRIAN ARMY): Original AUSTRIAN ARMY, bounded to the engagement. The Ministry of Culture identifies the opposing command under Clerfayt; this label does not incorporate the entire coalition or add the separate Maubeuge siege force.

The French republican infantry component uses the reviewed 1792–1803 cocked-hat, blue-coat and flintlock family. Lesueur’s contemporary volunteers and museum weapon evidence support this equipment analogy, not one outfit shared by every soldier. The 1837 Lami painting is not used as contemporary uniform evidence. The opposing aggregate has no equipment assignment in this review. The local participant ID, aggregate name, membership and CDB quantities remain unchanged. No infantry proportion or additional strength, casualty or death count is inferred.
